opennyai_summary.20_June_2023__facts:
This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.317/2022 dated 28.11.2022 registered at Police Station- Orchha Road, District- Chhatarpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 370,
372, 373, 376, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5L/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
opennyai_summary.20_June_2023__arguments:
applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
On the contrary, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
opennyai_summary.20_June_2023__ANALYSIS:
According to the prosecution case, 16 years old prosecutrix was missing on 11.09.2022 and recovered on 02.02.2023.
In this period of almost 5 months, she was not only sexually abused but also allegedly sold by persons involved in the crime.
According to the school record, date of birth of the prosecutrix was 20.08.2007 and in her statements recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has very clearly stated about the act of present applicant.
opennyai_summary.20_June_2023__decision:
Looking to the nature of crime committed by the applicant, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application stands rejected.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.317/2022 dated 28.11.2022 registered at Police Station- Orchha Road, District- Chhatarpur, for the offence punishable under Sections 363,
370, 372, 373, 376, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5L/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
The applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
H e further submits that the Jaggu @ Jagmohan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127060063/
1 prosecutrix and her parents have been examined before the trial Court and they have turned hostile,
did not support the prosecution story.
On the contrary, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
The earlier bail application of the applicant was dismissed on merits under M.Cr.C. no.18986/2023 on the ground that applicant was involved in sexually abusing and selling the minor prosecutrix.
The bail application has been argued on the ground that co-accused Babulal has already been released on bail under M.Cr.C. No.37751/2023.
The role of the present applicant can be put on parity with the role played by the co-accused Babulal.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
The order passed therein is enclosed along with the bail application.
Thus, applying the principles of parity,
the bail application is allowed.
It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE DevS Jaggu @ Jagmohan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127060063/
